system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}

Trial: CLEAR Outcomes NCT02993406 - Evaluation of Major Cardiovascular Events in Participants With, or at High Risk for, Cardiovascular Disease Who Are Statin Intolerant Treated With Bempedoic Acid (ETC-1002) or Placebo
Investigational drug: bempedoic acid
Document: Bempedoic Acid in the Treatment of Patients with Dyslipidemias and Statin Intolerance (journal, published 2021-01-27, source pmid:33502687)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
Bempedoic Acid in the Treatment of Patients with Dyslipidemias and Statin Intolerance

An elevated plasma low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) level is a well-established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ACSVD) risk factor. Randomized studies with statins (alone or in combination with other lipid-lowering drugs) have demonstrated their clinical efficacy in lowering LDL-C. Several classes of new, non-statin agents have been successfully studied and used (e.g., ezetimibe and inhibitors of proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 [i-PSCK9]). However, many high ACSVD risk patients remain at a high residual cardiovascular risk, with at least 10% being statin intolerant. Bempedoic acid (ETC-1002) is a new inhibitor of cholesterol synthesis that targets ATP citrate lyase (ACL). Importantly, ETC-1002 is only converted into an active form in the liver and is free of muscle side effects.Area Covered: Mechanism of action of ETC-1002, clinical pharmacology, completed clinical studies with bempedoic acid, lipid-lowering efficacy/safety issues, and recent meta-analyses of trials with ETC-1002.Expert Opinion: ETC-1002 has been extensively studied in phase I-III clinical studies in over 4000 individuals from different patient populations (statin intolerance, familial hypercholesterolemia, and high ACSVD risk patients), ETC-1002 has been demonstrated to have moderate cholesterol-lowering efficacy and a good safety profile at a dose of 180 mg/day as a monotherapy and in combination with statins and ezetimibe. The ongoing study CLEAR Outcomes, with composite cardiovascular endpoints, will elucidate the role of bempedoic acid in the management of high ACSVD risk and statin-intolerant patients with hypercholesterolemia. Long-term safety data on bempedoic acid are needed to fully establish this agent in evidence-informed guidelines for managing of patients with dyslipidemias.
--- END ---
